cells.tense: You are holding your chosen direction quietly, with the pen in hand, right here.
cells.act: hold your shape under the weight
cells.ask: Take the thing you've taken on and hold it without tightening — same shape, same grip, no extra force. Let it be heavy without letting the load change how you stand.
cells.core:
What you're aimed at is genuinely yours, and you're carrying it without gripping the rails. The ability to say this, not that, and mean it, is intact. Nothing in you is straining to prove the choice was right, and that steadiness is the whole asset — from there the direction keeps getting picked fresh rather than defended.

Something you've picked up will get heavier this week. Hold your form under it and don't add force, don't tighten your grip to look certain. The pull toward what you want stays light enough to steer by; it's the load that asks for endurance now. Carry it at the size it actually is, and don't make the steering harder than it is.
cells.sheetLine: You steer by what you want and hold your shape.
cells.verb: directing your energy by a chosen light
cells.place: under the pull of what you actually want

cells.tense: You will be forcing the outcome, bracing against a future you cannot write in ahead of time.
cells.act: draw the whole arrangement you are inside, with yourself marked on it
cells.ask: Draw the setup you're standing in — the goal, the people, the moving pieces — and mark yourself on the page. Look at it but decide nothing yet.
cells.core:
A want is steering you, and you're ahead of it — pushing at how it should go, checking outcomes that haven't happened, white-knuckling the timing. From outside it looks like strength; from inside it's the constant work of making tomorrow land before it can. What you're aimed at isn't in question. The grip on it is.

Pull back far enough to see the whole setup you're inside — the goal, the people in it, the moving parts — and mark where you stand in it. Not to judge it, just to see it. What you force looks urgent from close up and looks like one piece of a larger pattern from a step away. The direction survives being seen whole; usually it comes out cleaner.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding a future that can't be held yet.
cells.verb: directing your energy by a chosen light
cells.place: under the pull of what you actually want

cells.tense: You had stopped steering and left the direction standing at a door now behind you.
cells.act: do one thing today the way only you do it, and do not explain it
cells.ask: Do some everyday task your own way — as you'd actually do it — and don't explain or defend the choice to anyone afterward. That's all it takes.
cells.core:
You stopped steering a while back, and it's been some time since you picked a direction and meant it. Not because you stopped wanting things — the direction turned and you didn't, and now the wheel sits where you left it. From where you are it reads as not being someone who gets to steer, as if the last turns proved the wheel doesn't answer.

What's dim here is the shine, not the pull. Do some everyday task your own way — not to prove the way is right, just because it's yours — and keep it from becoming an argument with anyone. A piece of your own method, done with nobody told, is yours in a way that can't be taken back. Steering doesn't need belief to restart; it needs one act nobody supervised.
cells.sheetLine: The wheel slipped from your hands a while back.
cells.verb: directing your energy by a chosen light
cells.place: under the pull of what you actually want

cells.tense: You are steering by habit while the pen is down in a room you are already writing.
cells.act: be what you already are, in your acts
cells.ask: Catch one choice as it happens — a yes, a no, something you'd do anyway — and know it's you doing it. No speech after; just know it.
cells.core:
Direction is happening, and it looks from the outside like a life being chosen — turns made, times spent, a course held. Inside, none of the turns have a name on them; the momentum does the steering and habit signs for it. That isn't a failure of will. It's will running without anyone's hand on it, and it reads like drifting because it is.

Catch one choice at the moment you make it — a yes, a no, something you'd do anyway — and know it's you who decided. Not a big one, and no speech about it afterward. The pull you steer by was yours to begin with; knowing one ordinary choice as yours stops the momentum from writing everything in your hand. Nothing changes but who's holding the pen.
cells.sheetLine: You're going where you chose, without noticing you chose.

cells.place: under the pull of what you actually want

attempts.check: The draft's shakiest claim is 'recognized, not given — remembered, not arrived': the record says the inspiration is re-found, but I can't say from a card alone that the person ever truly had it. A reader could fairly say they know exactly what they long for and still can't hold their grip on the days, which is why the Too Much core leans on the forcing rather than the wanting. The asks survive a wrong read — sitting with a want, drawing the arrangement, doing one thing your own way, holding without tightening all teach something regardless. The sentence that serves the writing more than the person is any line about 'the light you're steering by'; I've cut every one of them.
